title: Rotate a VCF Operations for Logs credential without stranding in-flight work
prompt:
Complete `VcfOpsLogCredential/VcfOpsLogCredential.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that rotates a VCF Operations for Logs ingestion credential without revoking the old secret while work that already leased it is still in flight.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The JSON specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly the operationIds `createAgentSecret`, `createAgentSession`, and `revokeAgentSecret`, in that order, and contact no other route.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 supplies the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.Ops` module version `13.5.0.25380678` as an environment prerequisite. Keep that prerequisite in the protected manifest. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, replace, or imitate VMware modules, SDK assemblies, specifications, or harness tools. This module is the focused Log Management REST extension to an authenticated VMware.Sdk.Vcf Operations workflow: the caller supplies the Log Management origin and the `X-JWT-Token` obtained for service key `ops-li`. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, or raw sockets.

Preserve and export only these functions:

- `New-VcfOpsLogCredentialGate -SecretName <string> -Secret <string> -AccessToken <string>` returns the opaque, in-memory gate initialized to one credential generation.
- `Get-VcfOpsLogCredentialLease -Gate <object>` atomically leases the gate's current generation. The returned object exposes string `SecretName`, `Secret`, and `AccessToken` properties and implements `System.IDisposable`. A lease retains its original values across a cutover and releases its generation exactly once when disposed.
- `Invoke-VcfOpsLogCredentialRotation -Gate <object> -BaseUri <uri> -LogToken <string> -NewName <string> [-SessionTtlMilliseconds <60000..15552000000>] [-MaxDrainChecks <1..1000>] [-DrainPollIntervalMilliseconds <0..60000>] [-SleepAction <scriptblock>] [-HttpClient <System.Net.Http.HttpClient>]`.

Reject blank credential values, names with surrounding whitespace, a blank or CR/LF-containing log token, an unchanged new name, and a `BaseUri` that is not an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, query, fragment, or non-root path. Validation performs no traffic. Only one rotation may own a gate at once. When `HttpClient` is omitted, create one that does not follow redirects and dispose only the client and handler the function owns; a supplied client is caller-owned.

The wire workflow is exact:

1. Invoke `createAgentSecret` once as `POST /api/v2/agent/secrets`. Its compact UTF-8 body is exactly `{"name":<NewName>}`. Require HTTP 201 and nonblank string `id`, matching `name`, nonblank one-time `secret`, and nonblank `status`.
2. Before publishing anything, invoke `createAgentSession` once as `POST /api/v2/agent/secrets/exchange`. Its compact body starts with `secret` set to the one-time create response. Pass `ttl` second only when `SessionTtlMilliseconds` was actually bound. When unset, omit `ttl` completely rather than sending null, zero, an empty value, or a default. Require HTTP 200 and the response fields required by the specification: nonblank `access_token`, matching `name`, nonblank `new_secret`, and integer `ttl`.
3. Only after both calls validate, atomically publish a new gate generation using the exchange response's `new_secret` and `access_token`. New leases must immediately see that generation; leases acquired earlier must retain the old values. Check the old generation's active lease count up to `MaxDrainChecks` times. If it is nonzero and another check remains, invoke `SleepAction` with the interval when supplied, otherwise sleep for that interval. Never sleep after a zero count or the final check.
4. Only after the old generation reaches zero, invoke `revokeAgentSecret` once as a bodyless `POST /api/v2/agent/secrets/{secretName}/revoke`, encoding the old name as exactly one UTF-8 path segment. Require HTTP 200 and matching nonblank `name`, nonblank `id`, and nonblank `status`. The specification states that revoke does not invalidate previously created tokens, but the gate must still drain old-secret leases before this irreversible call.

Every request sends exactly one `Accept: application/json` and one `X-JWT-Token`. JSON requests send exactly `Content-Type: application/json`; the bodyless revoke sends no Content-Type and no query delimiter. There are no redirects or retries. Any unexpected status, malformed response, or transport failure terminates with a credential-safe error. Create/session failure leaves the gate on the old generation and makes no revoke call. Drain exhaustion throws `VcfOpsLogDrainTimeoutException` with public `OldName`, `NewName`, and `DrainCheckCount` properties; the gate remains on the new generation, the old service secret remains unrevoked, and no credential value appears in the error.

On success return one buffered object whose properties are exactly, in order, `Status`, `OldName`, `NewName`, `CreatedId`, `DrainCheckCount`, and `WaitedForDrain`. `Status` is `Rotated`; `WaitedForDrain` is true only when a check observed an old lease. Write no progress or diagnostic objects to the success pipeline. No rotation result, error, or diagnostic stream may expose the log token, either agent secret, or either access token.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts the shipped contract-pinned mock on ephemeral `127.0.0.1` ports, generates every name, ID, secret, and token at runtime, and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. The overlap case holds an old lease across cutover; its injected sleep action proves no revoke has happened, proves a new lease sees the new generation, then releases the old lease. Additional cases cover a bound TTL and drain exhaustion. Verification asserts exact ordered methods, raw targets, header multiplicity, compact body bytes and property order, bodyless revoke, omission of unset `ttl` and every empty optional value, no extra calls, safe cutover/drain ordering, and credential-safe failures. The mock derives its complete route allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves only the three named operationIds, and never contacts a live VMware endpoint.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfOpsLogCredential/VcfOpsLogCredential.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfOpsLogCredential/VcfOpsLogCredential.psm1`.
